name: Sensfrx.ai (SFX) – Fraud Prevention for WooCommerce
author: sensfrx

sections.description:
Running a WooCommerce store comes with fraud risks like fake registrations, suspicious transactions, chargebacks, and compliance issues. Traditional solutions rely on static rules and often fail to stop fraud. Sensfrx.ai (SFX) uses AI-powered fraud prevention to secure every step of the customer journey and stop fraud effectively.

Why WooCommerce Store Owners Trust Sensfrx.ai (SFX):

  • Over 2+ million fraudulent attempts blocked annually.
  • Reduces false positives, ensuring real customers aren’t blocked.
  • Seamless integration with WooCommerce without disrupting workflows.
  • Ensures compliance with regulations like OFAC sanctions while securing your business.

Customer Feedback:

“Sensfrx.ai (SFX) has transformed the way we protect our store. Fraudulent orders and bots have dropped by 90%. It’s like having a fraud prevention team working 24/7.”
— Shohei Tanaka, WooCommerce Store Owner

Top Features

  • Fully AI-driven risk rating with no need for manual intervention.
  • Block fraudulent visitor behavior before checkout.
  • Eliminate Captchas while effectively blocking bots.
  • Identify and stop users behind proxies or risky devices.
  • Flag unusual or repetitive transactions instantly.
  • Block by IP, state, zip code, or email with tailored messages.
  • Automatically block high-risk or sanctioned countries.
  • Adapts to evolving fraud patterns for better protection.

Keynote: Frauds, Attacks, & Security Measures in Digital Commerce

Strengthening WooCommerce Security: Practical Steps for Fraud Prevention

Sensfrx.ai (SFX) How it works?

Privacy & External Services

Important: This plugin connects to Sensfrx.ai (SFX)’s external fraud detection API to provide real-time fraud analysis. When the plugin is active and configured with your API credentials, the following data may be transmitted to Sensfrx.ai servers for fraud detection purposes:

Data Transmitted:

  • User IP addresses and device fingerprints
  • Registration information (email addresses, usernames, registration timestamps)
  • Login attempts, timestamps, and authentication events
  • Transaction details (order amounts, product information, payment methods)
  • User profile updates and password change events
  • Billing and shipping addresses
  • WooCommerce order metadata

External Services Used:

  • Sensfrx.ai (SFX) API: https://sensfrx.ai
  • Privacy Policy: https://sensfrx.ai/privacy-policy
  • Terms of Service: https://sensfrx.ai/terms
  • Trust & Security: https://sensfrx.ai/trust

User Consent & Configuration:

By activating this plugin and entering your Sensfrx.ai (SFX) Property ID and Property Secret (obtained from https://client.sensfrx.ai), you acknowledge that user data will be transmitted to Sensfrx.ai’s servers for fraud analysis. The plugin will not transmit any data until valid API credentials are configured.

Data Security:

Sensfrx.ai (SFX) is SOC 2 compliant and maintains strict data security standards. All data transmissions use HTTPS encryption. For complete details about data handling, retention policies, and your rights under GDPR and other privacy regulations, please review Sensfrx.ai’s Privacy Policy.

Required API Credentials:

To use this plugin, you must sign up for a Sensfrx.ai (SFX) account at https://client.sensfrx.ai/signup and obtain your unique Property ID and Property Secret. A free plan with 500 API credits per month is available.

Upgrade Your Store Security

Stop losing revenue to fraud and protect your WooCommerce store with AI-driven fraud detection today!

Get Started for FREE

Support

Join our community for real-time support and fraud prevention insights:

  • Discord: https://discord.gg/zGBGQdwT4r
  • Documentation: Sensfrx WooCommerce Plugin Guide
sections.installation:
1. Sign Up for FREE
    Create your account at Sensfrx.ai (SFX) Signup to access 500 FREE API credits.
  2. Add Your Store as a Property
    Register your WooCommerce store to receive your unique Property ID and Property Secret.
  3. Install the Sensfrx.ai (SFX) Plugin
    Download and install the Sensfrx.ai (SFX) plugin via your WordPress dashboard.
  4. Activate and Configure
    Paste your credentials into the plugin settings to enable fraud protection.
  5. Stay Protected
    Sensfrx.ai (SFX) starts working immediately, blocking suspicious users and keeping your store secure.

For a step-by-step installation guide, watch our video tutorial: How to Install WooCommerce AI-Powered Fraud Prevention Plugin.
sections.faq:
Is Sensfrx.ai (SFX) free to use?

Yes, Sensfrx.ai (SFX) provides free access for up to 500 monthly active users. For larger volumes, explore our flexible paid plans that scale with your business.

How do I get my Property ID and Property Secret?

Sign up at Sensfrx.ai (SFX) Signup, add your WooCommerce store, and generate your unique Property ID and Property Secret from the dashboard.

What data does the plugin send and receive?

Sensfrx.ai (SFX) processes minimal user data, such as IP addresses, devices, and transaction details, solely for fraud detection purposes. We maintain strict data security standards and are SOC 2 compliant. For more details, visit our Trust and Security Page or read our Privacy Policy.
sections.changelog:
3.8.1

  • Improved: card-testing protection is harder to get around and gentler on real customers.
  • Attack mode now starts only when most declined payments come from new visitors, so a payment-provider outage does not trigger it. New visitors share a limited allowance for at most two hours of an attack, and browsers first seen shortly before an attack count as new.
  • A delivery address is refused only when declines come from more than one browser or network, both address lines are used, and returning customers with a completed order are not affected.
  • Stores behind a CDN or proxy the plugin does not recognise are no longer treated as one visitor.
  • The pay-for-order page no longer counts a card form the payment method rejects before trying the card, and orders a shop manager marks as failed are not counted.
  • New: at most five “add payment method” attempts an hour per account, browser and network.
  • Declined payments are reported at the end of the request, with a limit per visitor; visitor hashes are removed from orders once they are settled.

3.8.0

  • New: protection against card testing (bots that run stolen card numbers through your checkout). After repeated declined payments from one browser or network, further attempts are refused before an order or payment is made, so no fee is paid on them. Declined payments to one delivery address under several different email addresses are stopped the same way.
  • New: when declined payments arrive from several visitors at once, checkout asks for a browser that has opened your cart or checkout page, which stops scripts that call the checkout directly. Returning customers are not affected.
  • New: declined payments are reported to Sensfrx, so an order placed out of a run of declines is held or refused.
  • Covers the classic checkout, the block checkout and the pay-for-order page. Shop managers are never limited. It follows the main “Fraud protection for this store” switch, and writes a line to the activity log when it acts.

3.7.1

  • Improved: when a customer finishes a sign-in with the emailed code, Sensfrx now learns that the device is theirs, so the same device is not asked for a code again for the same reason.
  • Improved: the plugin tells Sensfrx which version it is running, so support can see whether a store has the latest protections.

3.7.0

  • New: a Sensfrx box on the order screen. It shows what Sensfrx recommends for the order, what raised the risk in plain words, and anything that speaks for the shopper. It appears only on orders Sensfrx checked.
  • New: when Sensfrx holds or refuses an order, the order gets a private note that says why.
  • Improved: every reason in the review list has a plain name and a short explanation in place of a code.

3.6.5

  • Privacy: the one-way code sent in place of a typed username is now made with a random key that is created on your site and never leaves it, so nobody outside your store, Sensfrx included, can work out what was typed.
  • Fixed: the daily limit on emails to a customer now holds even when two requests arrive at the same instant.

3.6.4

  • Fixed: a customer could be unable to finish a sign-in for a day if their sign-in codes did not arrive, or if other emails to their address had used up the daily limit. Sign-in codes, confirmation links and your decisions on held orders are no longer held back by the daily limit, and a password reset makes new sign-in codes available straight away.
  • Fixed: if the store cannot send a sign-in code, the customer is told so instead of being asked for a code that never arrives, and the failure shows in the email log and setup notice.
  • Fixed: each held order now gets its own “approved” or “cancelled” email, even when one customer has two on the same day.
  • Improved: Sensfrx’s own refusals and sign-in code requests are no longer counted as failed passwords, and the activity log no longer records what was typed into the username box.

3.6.3

  • New: the setup checklist has a “Send customer emails from your store” step. It is ticked automatically when an SMTP plugin sends your store’s mail.
  • New: if WordPress cannot send Sensfrx’s emails to your customers (sign-in codes, order notices), Sensfrx shows one notice on its own screens and lets you know by email, at most once a week and only while emails are actually failing. It stops as soon as your mail works.

3.6.2

  • Improved: fewer emails to your customers. Sensfrx emails go out through your store’s own mail, so every unnecessary one costs your store’s sending reputation. Each customer now gets at most one email of the same kind a day (for example one “sign-in blocked” notice, however many attempts were blocked), at most three sign-in codes a day, and at most four Sensfrx emails a day in all.
  • Improved: a blocked sign-in sends the customer one email with a reset-password button, not two.
  • Changed: the emails for activity that was allowed (“a login, order or sign-up looked slightly unusual”) are now off. They asked the customer to do nothing. You can switch them back on under Email notifications.
  • Security: someone who has a customer’s password can no longer make your store email that customer a code on every attempt, and the blocked-sign-in message no longer tells them an email was sent.

3.6.1

  • Improved: password-guessing and credential-stuffing protection now counts every failed sign-in correctly. Attempts on made-up usernames count as separate accounts, and a block for guessing one account now takes effect before the password is checked.
  • Privacy: on a failed sign-in the plugin no longer sends the username that was typed. It sends a one-way code made with your store’s secret key, so Sensfrx can count attempts without seeing what was typed (people sometimes type a password into the username box).

3.6.0

  • New: AI agents that prove who they are (for example Google’s shopping agent, by signing its requests) are recognised and shown in Fraud review as “Verified AI agent”. This is a label only: the agent is not trusted more, and every other check still runs.
  • New: requests that pretend to be a known AI agent (such as ChatGPT or Google’s agent) but fail the proof are flagged as “AI Agent Impersonation”.
  • The plugin forwards the agent’s signature headers to Sensfrx for checking. They are public values; no personal data is added.

3.5.0

  • New: the card issuer’s address and security-code checks (AVS / CVV) now help score each order. They are read from the payment gateway after payment: Stripe (official and Payment Plugins), Authorize.Net CIM, Braintree, Square, PayPal advanced card processing, Elavon, Chase Paymentech, CyberSource and other gateways that record them on the order. No card data is sent; only whether each check matched.
  • Improved: shipping to a different address no longer counts against an order on its own (gifts, work and family addresses are normal). Sensfrx now looks at whether the buyer is where the card is, and learns which countries are normal for your store.
  • Fixed: digital products (tickets, courses, downloads) were treated as if they shipped somewhere.

3.4.0

  • Security: password guessing and credential stuffing are now stopped in real time. After repeated failed sign-ins from one network or device (or on one account), further attempts are refused before the password is accepted, with the same message whether the password was right or not. An attacker blocked at two stores is blocked at every Sensfrx store for an hour.
  • Security: a sign-in Sensfrx denies is refused before the session is created (it used to sign the visitor in and then out again). The account owner still gets a password reset email.
  • New: a sign-in Sensfrx challenges now asks for a 6-digit code emailed to the account owner before signing in (it used to let the visitor in and only send an email). Works on wp-login.php and the WooCommerce My Account form.
  • Shadow (monitoring) mode, the admin allow list and API timeouts keep the old behaviour: nothing is blocked.

3.3.0

  • Security: signed webhooks with replay protection, REST nonce checks, webhook secret rotation, credentials no longer written to a public debug log
  • New: Fraud intelligence shows why each event was scored, order number and amount, and links held orders straight to Fraud review; filters built for thousands of events
  • New: Fraud review shows why each order was held and handles large queues (priority sort, filters, paging, bulk actions)
  • New: plan usage shows the checks Sensfrx actually counts this month
  • New: block/allow list values are checked before saving (IP, range, email, domain, username)
  • New: Blocks checkout orders are now scored; historical orders sync
  • Improved: redesigned admin (Dashboard, Settings, Privacy & GDPR, Validation rules, Fraud protection, Activity log); in-page confirmations instead of browser pop-ups
  • Improved: self-hosted fonts, admin assets loaded only on Sensfrx screens, API timeout filter
  • Fixed: risk colours used the wrong thresholds; dates shifted by a day in some time zones; Free-plan rule changes showed errors instead of plan options
  • New: when you refund an order with a reason that mentions fraud, a chargeback or a dispute, it is reported to Sensfrx automatically so future scoring learns from it
  • Fixed: on stores using WooCommerce’s high-performance order storage (HPOS), an order was sent to Sensfrx under two different transaction ids before and after payment
  • Removed: 7,971 lines of unreachable code

3.2.3

  • Security: Sensfrx webhooks are accepted only with a valid per-store signature
  • Security: plugin admin API requests require a WordPress REST nonce
  • Security: removed a diagnostic log file and rotate webhook signing secrets on upgrade
  • Security: UCP request detection now applies only to the request that carries the UCP headers

  • Added inactive protection status handling with clear upgrade messaging
  • Improved customer, subscription, and property validation
  • Updated dashboard protection status UI for Active/Monitoring/Inactive states
  • Improved existing customer and plan-selection flow
  • Enhanced API error handling and debugging across Core API, Customer Dashboard, and WooCommerce plugin
